verdict: Texas Instruments grew revenue 10% to $4.42B as Analog sales rose 14%, and operating profit climbed 7% — though a bigger tax bill left net income a touch lower at $1.16B.

segments.name: Analog
segments.note: Analog chips — sensing and power products used in nearly every electronic device.

segments.name: Embedded Processing
segments.note: Processors that sit inside cars, appliances and factory equipment.

segments.name: Other
segments.note: DLP products, calculators and custom chips.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: R&D — designing new analog and embedded chips; up 6% from $491M a year ago.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Sales, marketing and the back office (SG&A); flat vs $446M a year ago.

opex.name: Restructuring charges/other
opex.note: Restructuring charges and other items; none a year ago. TI reports these inside its 'Other' segment result.

otherDetail: Other income (expense), net was $40M, less $141M of interest and debt expense — a net $101M expense outside operations.
oneTimers: Earnings per share included a 6-cent reduction that was not in the company's original guidance, as stated in the release.
The $32M of restructuring charges/other is reported inside the 'Other' segment, whose operating profit fell to $7M from $82M a year ago.
footerNote: Segment operating profit: Analog $1,395M, Embedded Processing $71M, Other $7M.

takeaways.title: Analog did the lifting
takeaways.text: Analog revenue rose 14% to $3.62B — 82% of all sales — while Embedded Processing grew 8% to $662M and Other fell 34% to $146M.

takeaways.title: Margins eased
takeaways.text: Gross margin slipped to 55.9% from 57.8% a year ago, but the revenue growth still lifted operating profit 7% to $1.47B.

takeaways.title: Cash returned to owners
takeaways.text: TI returned $1,693M in the quarter — $1,290M of dividends and $403M of buybacks — against $1,329M of free cash flow.

follow100Note: Rows are rounded to cents, so the waterfall lands a cent above the $26.29 kept as profit.
